question: Pick the project you are proudest of. What was the hardest technical trade-off you made, and what did you give up?
expectedSignals: Names concrete alternatives that were considered
Explains the decision criteria (performance, cost, time, team skills)
Acknowledges the downside that was accepted
Reflects on whether the trade-off held up

question: In one of your projects, why did you choose the database and overall architecture you did? What would make you choose differently?
expectedSignals: Ties choices to access patterns and data shape
Compares at least one realistic alternative
Identifies the conditions under which the choice would change

question: Imagine one of your projects suddenly has 100 times more users. What breaks first, and how would you fix it?
expectedSignals: Identifies the first realistic bottleneck rather than listing buzzwords
Proposes measurement before optimisation
Suggests targeted fixes such as caching, indexing, queues or horizontal scaling
Mentions the cost or complexity of each fix

question: Tell me about the worst bug you hit in one of your projects. How did you find the root cause?
expectedSignals: Describes a systematic debugging approach (reproduce, isolate, hypothesise)
Uses concrete tools such as logs, debugger or profiler
Explains the actual root cause, not just the symptom
Mentions what was done to prevent recurrence

question: What would you build differently if you started your main project again today, and why?
expectedSignals: Honest critique of their own design
Explains what they learned that changed their view
Prioritises the changes that matter most

question: Which part of your project did you personally design and build end to end? Walk me through a key decision in that part.
expectedSignals: Clearly separates personal contribution from team work
Explains a decision in technical depth
Shows ownership of the outcome, including follow-up after launch

question: Did anyone other than you use your project? What did you change based on their feedback?
expectedSignals: Mentions real users or reviewers and how feedback was gathered
Describes a concrete change driven by feedback
Shows prioritisation of feedback rather than doing everything

question: How did you know your project actually worked? Describe your testing approach and one bug your tests caught.
expectedSignals: Describes a mix of test levels (unit, integration, end-to-end) with reasons
Explains what was deliberately not tested and why
Gives a concrete example of a bug caught by tests
Mentions automation such as CI
